8.summary: Lindsey Stirling - The Snow Waltz Tour
8.description: Lindsey Stirling brings her spectacular Snow Waltz Tour to State Farm Center this holiday season. The award-winning violinist, dancer and entertainer delivers a one-of-a-kind holiday experience featuring breathtaking choreography, stunning visuals and Lindsey’s genre-defying arrangements of holiday classics and original music. Blending classical violin with electronic, pop and rock influences, Stirling has created a live show unlike anything else — combining virtuosic musicianship with dance, theatrical production and aerial performance. Her annual holiday tour has become a seasonal tradition, bringing the music of her acclaimed Christmas albums Warmer in the Winter and Snow Waltz to life on stage. $1 per ticket goes towards Lindsey’s foundation, The Upside Fund, which focuses on equitable healthcare and medical debt relief, mental health access, and nutrition education and food justice.
8.location: State Farm Center 1800 S 1st St, Champaign, IL 61820

38.summary: Sunday Salon: Maxwell Schultz, cello & Ana Huerta, piano
38.description: Krannert Center is proud to welcome the 2nd and 3rd-place winners of our 2026 Debut Artists Competition, cellist Maxwell Schultz and pianist Ana Huerta, to our Sunday Salon series this Sunday, November 1, featuring a program of Schumann and Brahms. Second-place winner Maxwell Schultz is an emerging cellist from the Chicago area. A former member of the Chicago Youth Symphony Orchestra, Schultz holds a master’s in performance from the University of Illinois where he is currently pursuing his Artist Diploma under the instruction of Jupiter String Quartet cellist, Daniel McDonough. He has performed as a featured soloist at festivals such as Domaine Forget de Charlevoix and Orford Musique and was a 2026 Young Artist at the prestigious Kneisel Hall Chamber Music School and Festival. Schultz will be accompanied by South Korean pianist Chanmi Lee, who is pursuing a Doctor of Musical Arts in Piano Performance and Literature at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, studying with Professor Timothy Ehlen. An accomplished soloist and collaborative musician, she has performed as a chamber musician and accompanist with the university’s Black Chorus. Third-place winner Ana Huerta is a Spanish pianist, collaborative artist, and scholar dedicated to creating musical experiences that foster connection, curiosity, and engagement. An award-winning soloist and active chamber musician, Huerta is co-founder of the saxophone-piano ensembles Dúo Índice and Atlantic Duo, that have recently joined forces as the newly formed Triskelion Trio. She is currently pursuing a Doctor of Musical Arts in Piano Performance and Literature with a cognate in Instrumental Conducting at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, studying under Dr. Chi-Chen Wu and serving as a Graduate Teaching Assistant in Collaborative Piano. Program: Robert Schumann (1810-1856) Sonata No. 1 in F-sharp minor, Op. 11 Ana Huerta, piano (approx. 33-minutes) Intermission Johannes Brahms (1833-1897) Sonata in D Major for Cello and Piano, Op. 78 Maxwell Schultz, cello Chanmi Lee, piano (approx. 30 minutes)
38.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

47.description: Experience the fellowship of communal dance with professionally trained dance instructors Laura Chiaramonte (Dance at Illinois) and Kate Insolia. If you or a loved one is living with Parkinson’s, join us to explore gentle movement in a safe and welcoming environment. No dance experience is needed! Set to uplifting, familiar music, provided by accompanist Beverly Hillmer, this class lasts approximately 70 minutes and may assist with the preservation and improvement of balance, flexibility, and strength. Please dress comfortably for this full-body workshop. If you have questions, please email krannertcenter [at] illinois.edu or phone 217.244.3963. Spaces with meters require payment even if accessible plates or hangtags are displayed. ▪ All other spaces in the underground garages are reserved on weekdays for permit holders. University of Illinois Parking patrols the lot regularly and will ticket anyone who is parked in a non-metered space without a paid lot permit. Presented in partnership with Dance at Illinois. This workshop was developed by the Mark Morris Dance Group, the Unity Parkinson’s Disease Support Group, Carle Clinic, Dance at Illinois, and Krannert Center.

55.description: The "Greatest Movie Musical of All Time" is faithfully and lovingly adapted by Broadway legends Betty Comden and Adolph Green, from their original award-winning screenplay in Singin' in the Rain . 60.summary: ECHOES Across the Atlantic | APOLLO'S FIRE
60.description: Apollo’s Fire conductor and harpsichordist Jeannette Sorrell, praised as "a master musical storyteller" (Seen & Heard International, UK) and known for her compelling explorations of multicultural influences in early music, creates timely programs that ask us to ponder our shared history. As the Grammy-winning baroque ensemble returns to Krannert Center, legendary Trinidadian soprano Jeanine De Bique joins them to explore the historical connections between Europe and the Caribbean colonies in the 18th century. Across the waters, tales of love, despair, and resilience emerge from the palaces of Europe and the plantations of the Caribbean—with surprising resonance for today. The virtuoso music of Handel, Purcell, Rameau, and Vivaldi meets the soulful voices of Caribbean poets in this celebration of our shared humanity.
60.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

62.summary: Aga Khan Master Musicians with Vincent Peirani, accordion
62.description: Join the Aga Khan Master Musicians for an extraordinary evening of musical innovation and cultural dialogue. Brought together by the Aga Khan Music Programme, this acclaimed ensemble unites elite performers and composer-arrangers whose artistry is rooted in the traditions of the Middle East, Mediterranean Basin, Central Asia, and China. Blending canonical forms with contemporary expression, the Master Musicians create a vibrant, original sound that honors heritage while embracing new creative possibilities. Featuring virtuoso accordion player Vincent Peirani, the ensemble is completed with distinguished artists Wu Man on pipa (a four-stringed Chinese lute), Basel Rajoub on saxophone, Feras Charestan on qanun (a Middle-Eastern zither), Abbos Kosimov on doira (Uzbek frame drum), and Yurdal Tokcan on oud in a program showcasing exceptional mastery and cross-cultural collaboration transcending boundaries and reimagining traditions. Due to unforeseen circumstances, cellist Vincent Ségal will not perform with the Aga Khan Master Musicians on the ensemble's November 2026 US Tour.
62.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

65.summary: Raphaël Feuillâtre: An ELLNORA Reverb Event
65.description: Considered the new global face of classical guitar, Raphaël Feuillâtre fascinates listeners with the depth of his interpretations, his dazzling technique, and the richness of his repertoire. Born in Djibouti and raised in Cholet, France, by immigrant parents, Feuillâtre began winning guitar competitions at age 18, graduated from the elite Paris Conservatoire, released his first recording at 23, and three years later signed a contract with Deutsche Grammophon, classical music’s most prestigious label. In 2023, he became the second-most listened-to classical artist on Apple Classical. This charismatic French guitarist with the creative vision required to make works from all periods sound as if they were written yesterday—alive, heartfelt, filled with color—notes: “My goal is always to allow the guitar to sing.”
65.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

68.description: Join us as we bring one of C-U's powerhouse voices to Krannert Center Uncorked on November 19! J'Lyn Hope is a multidisciplinary artist whose work explores the transformative power of imagination. Blending jazz, rock, soul, and improvisation, she creates dynamic musical experiences that blur the boundaries between sound, feeling, and discovery. Known for her expressive voice and magnetic energy, Hope uses her loop station to build intricate layers of music in real time, transforming her voice into rhythm, melody, harmony, and texture. She describes these creations as "sound paintings"—where the color of her voice follows the brushstrokes of her creativity. Her work is rooted in the belief that art is a powerful tool that encourages us to reach beyond our notions of what is possible, tapping into the magic of what lies beyond. The love, light, and hope infused throughout her art awaken the dreamer in us all. Come see J'Lyn Hope November 19 at Stage 5 in the Krannert Center lobby. Enjoy a beverage from our Stage 5 bar and connect with friends old and new. All Krannert Center Uncorked performances are free on select Thursdays from 5:30-7pm.

73.summary: Krannert Center Uncorked: Kurt Reeder Trio, A Charlie Brown Christmas
73.description: Join us as C-U's house keyboardist, Kurt Reeder, brings his trio to Krannert Center Uncorked for a special performance of pianist Vince Guaraldi's classic jazz recording "A Charlie Brown Christmas" on December 3. From Provo, Utah, Kurt came to the University of Illinois in 2018 to complete his Masters in Jazz Performance, fell in love with the community, and never left. Outside of his trio, he is part of several local ensembles, including The Kurt Reeder Organization, The Broadmoor Quartet, Allnighter, and others. He can be found performing at the Rose Bowl Tavern multiple nights a week. Joining Kurt as part of this acoustic jazz trio are two giants of the local music scene: veteran drummer extraordinaire Ian Shepherd (Ian Shepherd and Friends, 90s Daughter) and U of I alumni bassist and educator Dr. Emma Taylor (Emma Taylor Quartet, Simply This Quintet). Come enjoy a complete performance of this beloved jazz album, along with other select pieces from Guaraldi's catalog that fit the evening and the season. 77.description: Handel’s Messiah remains one of the most enduring and beloved works in the choral repertoire, offering a profound synthesis of musical beauty and spiritual reflection. In collaboration with the University of Illinois Choirs under the direction of Andrea Solya, Sinfonia da Camera presents this monumental work with a distinguished roster of soloists: soprano Ollie Watts Davis, mezzo-soprano Thereza Lituma, tenor John Swedberg, and bass Ricardo Herrera. From the celebratory brilliance of the “Hallelujah” chorus to the introspective lyricism of its arias, Messiah traverses a wide emotional and theological landscape. Its carefully crafted structure and expressive clarity exemplify Handel’s dramatic genius. This performance invites audiences to engage with a work that continues to inspire through its balance of grandeur, intimacy, and a timeless holiday message.
77.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

82.description: The Champaign-Urbana Symphony Orchestra’s popular holiday concert features seasonal favorites to please the whole family. The celebration begins with A Chanukah Overture by Robert Wendell and A Christmas Feast , a medley of five ancient carols arranged by Matthew Naughtin. Waldteuful’s lively classic, The Skaters’ Waltz , will brighten holiday spirits. Dazzling soprano Katelyn Lee performs Mozart’s radiant motet Exsultate Jubilate and Adolphe Adams’ beloved carol, “O Holy Night.” The magic continues as the talented singers of the Central Illinois Youth Chorus join the CUSO to perform Christmas Canon , the Trans-Siberian Orchestra’s beautiful interpretation of Pachelbel’s Canon in D . Naughtin’s A Visit from St. Nicholas presents a charming orchestral setting for Clement C. Moore’s well-known poem. Leroy Anderson’s “Sleigh Ride,” a visit from Santa, and a sing-along of holiday carols will make the season bright.
82.location: Krannert Center - Foellinger Great Hall, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

83.summary: Step Afrika! presents The Fruits of Our Labor
83.description: Celebrate the body as an instrument with Step Afrika!, the GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS™ title holder for the Largest Stepping Dance and the world’s leading authority on the art form of stepping. The company’s newest work, The Fruits of Our Labor , blends the power of body percussion and contemporary dance with the vibrant energy of isipantsula (a rhythmic dance originating in South African townships) and the South African gumboot dance. Long-time Step Afrika! collaborator Jakari Sherman and South African choreographer Vusi Mdoyi lead an ensemble of virtuosic dancers whose bodies become instruments—clapping, striking, and stepping in mesmerizing unison, merging rhythm and ritual, history and storytelling.
83.location: Krannert Center - Tryon Festival Theatre, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

84.summary: The Neo-Futurists present The Infinite Wrench
84.description: The Chicago-based Neo-Futurists have been writing and performing 30 plays in 60 minutes since 1988. Each play offers something different: be it funny, profound, elegant, disgusting, topical, irreverent, terrifying, or a song, all are original and truthful, tackling the here-and-now, and inspired by the lived experiences of the performers. “The ingenuity and engagement of the work not only remains but has deepened . . . the ensemble maps thorny social, psychological, and political terrain with foolishness and ferocity,” says the Chicago Reader . With new plays every week, The Infinite Wrench is The Neo-Futurists’ ongoing and ever-changing attempt to shift the conventions of live performance and speak to those unreached or unmoved by traditional theatre.
84.location: Krannert Center - Studio Theatre, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801

87.summary: Mark Morris Dance Group and Music Ensemble: Music at Play
87.description: With wit, exuberance, and an irresistible sense of play, the Mark Morris Dance Group brings together four works that showcase the humor, invention, and musical imagination of Mark Morris. Designed to delight audiences of all ages, this lively program combines brilliant dancing, vivid musicality, and theatrical surprise. In My Party , Morris transforms the familiar awkwardness and excitement of a youthful gathering into a tender and funny celebration of dancing together. The wonderfully offbeat Tamil Film Songs in Stereo Pas de Deux is pure cosmic invention propelled by the rhythms of South Indian popular music. Peccadillos , set to Erik Satie's miniature piano pieces originally written for children, finds humor and humanity in a whimsical solo filled with gesture, character, and imagination. And in Sport , Morris takes inspiration from Satie's playful Sports et divertissements , turning golf, swimming, tennis, and other athletic pursuits into a witty choreographic playground. Together, these four works offer an ideal evening of the Mark Morris Dance Group: sophisticated without being solemn, playful without ever losing artistry, and animated throughout by Morris' extraordinary ability to make music visible through dance. It is a program for longtime dance lovers, first-time audiences, children, parents, grandparents—and anyone who enjoys the pleasure of watching remarkable dancers have some serious fun.
87.location: Krannert Center - Tryon Festival Theatre, 500 S Goodwin Ave, Urbana, IL 61801
